2026 Ohio Estimated Income Tax Instructions
Do I Have To Make Estimated Payments?
If your income is subject to Ohio withholding, you generally do not
need to make estimated payments. You should make estimated
payments for tax year 2026 if your estimated Ohio tax liability (total
tax minus total credits) less Ohio withholding is more than $500.
Individuals generally must make estimated payments if they are:

Also, special rules regarding estimated payments apply to certain
taxpayers with farming and/or fishing income. See Adm. Code
5703-7-04.
If you do not make the required estimated payments, you may be
subject to an interest penalty for underpayment of estimated taxes.
See form IT/SD 2210.

 Employees who are under-withheld by their employers;

For more information, see the “Income - Estimated Income/School
District Taxes and the 2210 Interest Penalty” FAQ topic at tax.
ohio.gov/2210.

 Retirees without Ohio tax withholding from their pensions;

 Pass-through entity investors or sole proprietors; AND/OR
 Individuals with large amounts of investment income.

What Are My Payment Options?
Once you have calculated your estimated payments, you must pay
them quarterly through any of the following methods:

Estimated payments are due as follows:
1st quarter
2nd quarter
3rd quarter
4th quarter

-

April 15, 2026
June 15, 2026
Sept. 15, 2026
Jan. 15, 2027

 By

Electronic Check - Pay by electronic check using the
department’s OH|TAX eServices at tax.ohio.gov/pay. There is
no fee for using this payment method.

Use the Ohio Universal Payment Coupon (OUPC) to make
estimated Ohio income tax payments. Married taxpayers unsure
of their filing status for 2026 should make separate estimated
payments based on their individual estimated Ohio tax liabilities.
Estimated payments will only be applied to the return associated
with the Social Security number listed on the OUPC. Payments will
not be split between you and your spouse if you combine your tax
liabilities, but file separately.

 By Credit or Debit Card - Pay by credit or debit card using the

department’s OH|TAX eServices at tax.ohio.gov/pay. These
payments are processed by a third-party. The third-party will
charge your account a convenience fee. The state of Ohio does
not receive any of this fee.

 By Mail - Send a check or money order with the OUPC. Make the

payment payable to “Ohio Treasurer of State.”

Note: Instead of making estimated payments, you can increase your
Ohio withholding by filing a revised Ohio IT 4 with your employer.

*If line 3 of the worksheet above is $500,000 or greater, line 4 should be zero.
